To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single intranasal dose of influenza-based defective interfering (protecting) virus protected mice against lethal infection with influenza A virus from a different subtype and against lethal infection with a genetically unrelated virus, pneumonia virus.
a broad spectrum antiviral treatment is possible by using protecting influenza A virus, and this treatment is effective against both influenza A viruses and pneumoviruses.

we have developed a novel broad-spectrum antiviral therapy that can be used to protect against a variety of respiratory viruses, and that this therapy has the potential to prevent the emergence of antiviral resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the control of viral disease based on the use of protecting viruses.
the development of a novel broad-spectrum approach for the prevention of respiratory virus infections.
the development of a novel broad spectrum treatment for respiratory virus infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protecting virus approach provides a broad-spectrum protection against all interferon sensitive respiratory viruses and influenza A viruses.
protecting viruses are effective against all respiratory viruses, including influenza viruses, which are susceptible to type I interferon.
protecting influenza A viruses are effective in vivo against pneumovirus, a virus from a completely different virus family, and that protection against pneumoviruses is mediated by type I interferon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single dose of protecting influenza A virus provides broad-spectrum protection against influenza A viruses and pneumovirus infection.
we have shown that a single dose of protecting influenza virus protects against all interferon-susceptible respiratory viruses, including all influenza viruses.
a single dose of protecting influenza A virus protects against all interferon sensitive respiratory virus infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of protecting viruses may provide broad protection against a wide range of respiratory viruses.

the protecting viruses are a novel class of broad-spectrum antivirals that have the potential to protect not just against a single virus, as has been shown for the related defective interfering particles, but against a whole class of related viruses, and possibly unrelated viruses.
protecting virus is an attractive approach for developing broad-spectrum treatments for respiratory virus infections.
